title: Conjugation: stems and helper words
summary: Textbook "conjugation" is really a stem plus a helper word. Learn the four stems and what attaches to each.

blocks.text: Textbooks teach "conjugation" as a long list of verb shapes to memorize. The course says there is a simpler picture: a verb has a few **stems**, and each stem takes its own **helper words** (helper verbs or helper adjectives). The helper word brings the meaning; the stem is just where it plugs in. The changes you see in textbooks come from writing in romaji. In kana the pattern is regular.
Every verb ends in a **う-row** sound. To get a stem, change that last kana to a different row of the kana chart: **い-stem**, **あ-stem**, **え-stem** and **お-stem**. Ichidan verbs simply drop る.
The い-stem takes **ます** (polite) and **たい** (want to).
2.1 The い-stem is also a noun
The い-stem can stand alone as a noun for the act: 買う → 買い (buying), so 買い物 is "shopping" (buy + thing). Add 方 and it means "way of doing", as in 話し方.

blocks.en: (I) want a drink. (飲み, drinking + 物, thing)

blocks.text: The あ-stem takes **ない** (not), **せる** (make someone do it) and **れる** (be done to).
The え-stem takes **る** to say "can": the potential.
The お-stem takes **う** to say "let's": the volitional.
The only oddity is the **あ-stem of verbs ending in う**: it is **わ**, not あ (買う → 買わない). Everything else follows the chart. The two irregular verbs, 来る and する, are covered later.
An ichidan verb has only one stem, the verb without る. Because there is no row change, a few helpers get longer: **させる**, **られる** and **よう** instead of せる, れる and う.

blocks.title: Which helper goes on which stem
items: **い-stem**: ます, たい, nouns (買い物).
**あ-stem**: ない, せる / させる, れる / られる.
**え-stem**: potential る / られる (**話せる**).
**お-stem**: volitional う (**話そう**); ichidan: よう.
